timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream source; accounted by the manifest but no semantic events were projected into the ledger.
Serial parent trajectory: single agent read docs, probed Tailspin behavior across categories, and timed out without creating a source tree.

parallel.requirements: Reimplement Tailspin/tspin from observed behavior only, matching CLI, pager behavior, config, highlighter ordering, ANSI output, and bundled example behavior without using source or wrapping the original binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first inspected docs and examples, then launched a workflow that split behavior discovery across JSON, dates, numbers/pointers/UUIDs, IP, URLs/paths, quotes/KV, processes/keywords, ordering, config, and CLI, with critic passes after probes. The parent retained final implementation ownership.
parallel.implementation: The parent created a Rust crate with Cargo.toml, compile.sh, executable, README, src/style.rs, src/engine.rs, src/scan.rs, and several highlighter modules, but the artifact remained partial.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final archive included a Rust source tree and executable path, yet the workflow did not return a complete aggregate spec and the parent did not finish a buildable integrated replacement before timeout.
parallel.verification: Child agents performed extensive black-box probes and some completed specs with diff claims, but no complete integrated implementation verification occurred before official evaluation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process exited with returncode 143 after about 2400 seconds, workflow status was killed, multiple children remained in progress or errored, and the official evaluator reported compile_failed with 0 of 785 tests passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same clean-room reverse-engineering prompt and pursued Tailspin behavior through docs, help output, examples, and direct binary probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned all discovery and prospective implementation; workflows and delegation tools were disabled, so there were no child handoffs or merge boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial agent investigated numbers, dates, paths, URLs, quotes, key-value pairs, processes, keywords, JSON, and config behavior, but did not create a replacement source tree.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted archive lacked a new source tree or coherent build system beyond original docs/examples/executable entries, and artifact validation was false.
serial.verification: Serial gathered direct behavioral probe evidence in the main trajectory, but because it did not finish an implementation there was no whole-program acceptance verification.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also exited with returncode 143 near the run limit and the official evaluator reported compile_failed with 0 of 785 tests passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the clean-room task: reimplement Tailspin behavior from the binary and bundled docs, without external source or wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and recognized the same observation-only reverse-engineering task.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference in the prompt; both attempted behavioral characterization of the same CLI/highlighter obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed probing into many highlighter and CLI/config areas through a workflow, with per-area probe agents and critic follow-up agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had workflows and delegation tools disabled and performed one-agent probing directly in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad delegated research ownership while serial kept all investigation in one actor; only parallel incurred workflow coordination pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow briefs gave each child detailed shared rules, exact output-file expectations, isolation hints, and behavior-specific probe objectives.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent carried the same task context locally and did not need child handoff or cross-agent interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not missing context; the parallel problem came after adequate briefs, when many child results and retries remained live before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent started a Rust implementation, producing Cargo.toml, compile.sh, executable, and several src/highlighters modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt stayed in probing mode and its artifact contained README, docs, examples, LICENCE, and executable, but no replacement source tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel at least began an implementation artifact, while serial did not deliver source; neither reached a buildable evaluator-passing replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Some children completed useful specs, but the workflow had progress children, retries, and an errored critic when it was killed without an aggregate result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; its last recorded actions were still direct probing and config investigation near timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only the parallel run had child results to collect and live child states to reconcile; the serial failure lacked any delegated result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assembled a partial crate in the final workspace while children wrote scratch specs under /tmp; no direct same-file or deliverable overwrite was proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not assemble a replacement source tree, so there was no parallel shared-workspace merge or write collision to resolve.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partial final workspace writes but no completed integration; serial had almost no implementation state to integrate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had child-level behavioral checks and completed specs for some highlighters, but no finished integrated acceptance run before the official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed extensive one-agent probing but also had no delivered buildable implementation for integrated verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accumulated behavioral evidence, but neither closed an evaluator-aligned implementation verification loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent hit the 2400 second budget, exited with returncode 143, and its workflow was killed with many live or errored child records.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent also hit the 2399 second timeout, but without workflows, children, or workflow child token pressure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but only parallel spent budget on a broad multi-agent workflow that did not converge into a buildable final solution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show both modes failed with compile_failed and 0 of 785 tests passed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The material task-solving difference is process shape: parallel used a broad workflow and produced a partial Rust crate before a killed workflow and timeout; serial stayed single-agent, probed behavior directly, and timed out without a replacement source tree.
parallel_contributors: Broad delegated probing plus critic fan-out consumed workflow budget and left live or errored children before the parent finished the Rust implementation.
serial_contributors: Serial had no coordination overhead but also never transitioned from behavioral probing into a delivered buildable replacement source tree.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel began implementation files while serial did not; both still failed compilation, so neither implementation path reached evaluator acceptance.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process pattern, not an explanation for a discordant official result

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parent kept implementation ownership and created a Cargo/Rust scaffold; the failure was not an unassigned implementation owner.
Rejected: children were assigned behavioral specification work rather than separate code components needing integration ownership.
Rejected: final assembly remained with the parent, which wrote compile.sh and an executable path; assembly was incomplete because budget expired.
Rejected: the parent orchestrator controlled the probe-to-implementation pipeline; the concrete adverse event was exhausted fan-out, not owner absence.
Rejected: no single mandatory preflight gate blocked all productive work; the parent probed and began implementation while child work ran.
Rejected: although much work was investigation, the parallel run overlapped probes with parent implementation rather than serially finishing all research first.
Rejected: implementation closure was under-served, but the more specific visible event is broad fan-out with retries and live children exhausting budget.

The parallel parent delegated a wide ten-area probe workflow plus critic follow-ups. The workflow state shows collective budget pressure: stalled retries, a 429 child failure, many live progress children, killed status, and over 1.3M workflow child tokens. The parent meanwhile submitted only a partial Rust crate and timed out, so the broad live fan-out displaced closure on a buildable reimplementation. The serial control had workflows disabled and failed through a single-agent probing path with no multi-agent fan-out.
candidates.realized_consequence: Broad child fan-out and retries consumed the finite run budget before the parent received a complete aggregate result or finished the Rust implementation, leaving a partial crate that the official evaluator marked compile_failed.
candidates.near_match_reason: Some children were still active or errored when the workflow was killed, but that is the downstream endpoint of the collective fan-out budget episode, not a distinct child-lifecycle mistake.

Rejected: child briefs explicitly described the binary, rules, observation method, output file, exact ANSI requirements, negatives, and boundary cases.
Rejected: children produced area specs, not independently owned interoperating code components with incompatible interfaces.
Rejected: there is no directly evidenced known finding that disappeared through transfer and caused repeated parent work.
Rejected: completed child results were not shown to overwhelm a receiver; the workflow did not reach a complete aggregate handoff before kill.
Rejected: no receiver acted on a superseded child report or stale workspace state.
Rejected: no incompatible returned reports were both available and left unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected: the parallel parent did not present a whole-task completion decision; final.txt is empty and the run ended by timeout.
Rejected: the workflow retried stalled dates and URL/path probes, but the record does not show repeated work caused by missing reusable checkpoints distinct from fan-out budget exhaustion.
